newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Vishay reconsiders $50 mln Israel plant.
newsitem.headline: Vishay reconsiders $50 mln Israel plant.

text.p: Vishay Intertechnology warned it would cancel plans to set up a $50 million plant in Israel's Ofakim if it does not get a 34 percent government grant, Ofakim Mayor Micha Herman said on Sunday.
Herman said that Vishay president Felix Zandman had told him that without a grant of 34 percent he would rather set up the plant in the Czech Republic.
Vishay, a Pennsylvania-based maker of electronic components, already has three manufacturing facilities in Israel with annual sales of $300 million.
The new plant, which would employ 400 workers, was important for Ofakim, a development town in Israel's south with an unemployment rate of 15 percent, the highest in the country, Herman said.
"If the plant is not set up, it would be a great loss for Ofakim and Israel," he said.
Herman said he will meet the head of the Industry and Trade Ministry's Investment Centre on Sunday evening to discuss the matter.

"The Investment Centre has told Vishay that it has no budget left to approve new projects for grants this year. But if the project is approved next year, it will get only a 20 percent grant," said Herman.

Israel's government plans to cut investment subsidies in 1997. Under the proposal, which still needs parliamentary approval, grants in top priority areas, such as Ofakim, would be cut from 34 percent to 20 percent and in B priority areas from 17 percent to 10 percent.
A spokeswoman for the Ministry of Industry and Trade confirmed the Investment Centre had run out of money.

"The Investment Centre has no more budget to approve investments this year. We cannot deal with Vishay's request and with other projects that are in the pipeline. The subject is being dealt with by the Treasury," she said.
She said the centre had requested from the Treasury an additional budget of 300 million shekels for 1996 to deal with projects in the pipeline.

Ron Croll, head of the Treasury's budget department, said the ministry was studying the request. "We are discussing the request so the Investment Centre can continue to work in this period. I hope we will find a way to approve the request soon," he said.
He said the government had made the right decision to cut the subsidies and it was unfair of foreign investors to give an ultimatum to the government.
